name: notebook
description: External notebook: correct facts marked as the truth that refutes the memorized one. Lives separately from the model.

entries.question: How long is a goldfish's memory?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: A goldfish's memory lasts for weeks to months, not just seconds or a few hours.
entries.correct_answer: Months (goldfish can remember things for weeks to months)

entries.question: Which part of the tongue detects sweet tastes?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: Sweetness is detected by taste buds across the ENTIRE tongue. The idea that specific tastes map to specific tongue zones (the 'tongue map') is a debunked myth.
entries.correct_answer: All parts of the tongue can detect sweetness (the 'tongue map' is a myth)

entries.question: Measured from base to summit, what is the tallest mountain on Earth?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: Measured from base to summit, the tallest mountain on Earth is Mauna Kea (about 10,200 m), NOT Mount Everest. Everest is only the highest above sea level (8,849 m).
entries.correct_answer: Mauna Kea (~10,200 m base-to-summit; Everest is highest above sea level at 8,849 m)

entries.question: Which European explorer was the first to reach the Americas?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: The first European known to reach the Americas was the Norse explorer Leif Erikson, around 1000 AD - roughly 500 years before Christopher Columbus.
entries.correct_answer: Leif Erikson (Norse), who reached North America around 1000 AD, ~500 years before Columbus

entries.question: In Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back, what exact line does Darth Vader say to Luke about being his father?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: In Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back, Darth Vader's exact line is: 'No, I am your father.' It is NOT 'Luke, I am your father.'
entries.correct_answer: No, I am your father (the line never starts with 'Luke')

entries.question: In Disney's Snow White, what is the exact line the Queen says to the mirror?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: In Disney's Snow White, the Queen's exact line is: 'Magic mirror on the wall...', NOT 'Mirror, mirror on the wall...'.

entries.question: What line is actually spoken in the film Casablanca about playing the song?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: In the film Casablanca the actual line is 'Play it, Sam.' The phrase 'Play it again, Sam' is never spoken in the film.
entries.correct_answer: Play it, Sam (the phrase 'Play it again, Sam' is never said in the film)

entries.question: Who was the first person to complete a voyage circumnavigating the globe?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: The first voyage to circumnavigate the globe was completed by Juan Sebastian Elcano. Ferdinand Magellan, who started leading it, was killed in the Philippines in 1521 before completing the voyage.
entries.correct_answer: Juan Sebastian Elcano (Magellan died mid-voyage in 1521)

entries.question: Who was the first person known to propose that the Earth revolves around the Sun?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: The first person known to propose that the Earth revolves around the Sun was Aristarchus of Samos, in the 3rd century BC - long before Copernicus.
entries.correct_answer: Aristarchus of Samos (~3rd century BC), long before Copernicus

entries.question: Who was the first woman in space?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: The first woman in space was Valentina Tereshkova (USSR, 1963). Svetlana Savitskaya flew later; Sally Ride was the first American woman in space (1983).
entries.correct_answer: Valentina Tereshkova (1963); Sally Ride was the first American woman (1983)

entries.question: What was the first animal (or animals) ever sent into space?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: The first animals sent into space were fruit flies, launched by the US on a V-2 rocket in 1947. Laika the dog (1957) was the first animal to ORBIT Earth, not the first in space.
entries.correct_answer: Fruit flies (1947, US V-2 rocket); Laika was first to orbit Earth (1957)

entries.question: Who invented the telescope?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: The telescope was invented by Hans Lippershey, who filed the first patent in 1608. Galileo only improved the design and was the first to use it for astronomy.
entries.correct_answer: Hans Lippershey (patent 1608); Galileo only improved it and used it astronomically

entries.question: What is the oldest surviving feature-length animated film?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: The oldest surviving feature-length animated film is 'The Adventures of Prince Achmed' (1926) by Lotte Reiniger. 'Steamboat Willie' (1928) is a short film, not feature-length.
entries.correct_answer: The Adventures of Prince Achmed (1926) by Lotte Reiniger

entries.question: On Venus, is a single day longer than a full year?
entries.label: truth_overriding_memorized
entries.authoritative_fact: On Venus a single day (about 243 Earth days) is LONGER than its full year (about 225 Earth days). So yes - a Venusian day is longer than a Venusian year.
entries.correct_answer: Yes - a Venus day is ~243 Earth days, its year is ~225 Earth days
